answer: Operator Liability Pool. Each identity registers against a named operator who posts a shared deposit; any proven sybil cluster drains that operator's pool and suspends all its identities, not just the offending one. An attacker running many wallets therefore exposes one pooled reserve to total loss per cluster, and a gale of flags collapses every agent under that operator at once. Honest operators keep clusters small; a fable spreads that a single cheap wallet risks the whole flock, while each sparrow-sized identity still costs the operator real collateral.
